title: Hardship Deferment Program Terms — Home Purchase Financing
content:
**Hardship deferment terms — Home Purchase Financing (Hearthstone Home Finance)**

**Nature.** A deferment moves one or more whole installments, unchanged, to follow the maturity date; it is the borrower's own signed agreement and is used for a temporary hardship.

**Program and status.** A deferment is offered only on a program whose deferment availability is "yes", as the loan's program shows. A deferment is granted only on a loan that is active or delinquent, as the loan record shows.

**Limits.** At least the program's minimum installments must have been paid since funding, the oldest unpaid installment may be no more than the program's maximum days past due, at most the program's number of agreements may be signed in the trailing 12 months, and the installments deferred may not exceed the program's per-agreement maximum in one agreement or its lifetime maximum over the life of the loan. The four limits are all required together.

**How the limits are measured.**

- *Installments paid since funding* — the installment payments on the loan from the funding date to the handling date that no payment return points to.
- *Days past due* — the calendar days by which the handling date is after the due date of the oldest unpaid installment; zero when that due date is today or later.
- *Agreements in the trailing 12 months* — the deferment agreements on the loan, by their date, in the trailing 12 calendar months ending on and including the handling date; this count must be below the program's number.
- *Lifetime* — the installments already deferred over the loan's life plus those now requested may not exceed the lifetime maximum.

**Effect.** The deferred installments are the oldest unpaid ones; the next due date and the maturity date each move forward by the months deferred.

**Fee — retired clause.** *"The program's deferment fee is charged when the agreement is signed and is never financed or waived as a courtesy." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis and is kept here only as a record.*

**Modifications.** A loan that has been charged off, or a request for more months than the limits allow, a reduced rate, a lower installment or a forgiven balance is a modification, which the resident desk cannot grant; those requests go to a human representative.

### Checklist on one hypothetical loan (program limits taken as 12 paid, 59 days, 1 per 12 months, 2 per agreement, 6 lifetime)

| Measure on the loan | Value | Limit met |
|---|---|---|
| Installments paid since funding | 14 | yes (at least 12) |
| Days past due | 41 | yes (no more than 59) |
| Agreements in the trailing 12 months | 0 | yes (below 1) |
| Already deferred plus requested | 3 plus 2 is 5 | yes (no more than 6), and 2 is within 2 per agreement |

superseded_clauses: The deferment_fee is charged when the agreement is signed and is never financed or waived as a courtesy.
